title: How to Write Support Docs for AI
speakers_and_attribution: The opening speaker asks about writing support documentation for AI. An unidentified respondent answers from 00:00:24. Brief exchanges and closing recommendations follow from 00:02:14, but speaker boundaries are incomplete. The captions do not establish which speaker, if any, is Adam Robinson. All substantive advice is therefore attributed to unidentified speakers rather than treated as Adam's beliefs or achievements. Rob is mentioned as a tool creator; he is not securely identified as a speaker.
summary: The discussion recommends writing support documentation for both humans and AI through clear structure and explicit procedural text. It compares effective formatting with SEO practices and descriptive text with accessibility practices. Closing remarks recommend an existing knowledge base as a model and report that Rob created a specialized ChatGPT tool for optimizing articles. No personal history or quantified business results are supplied.

key_learnings.claim: Support articles should serve both AI systems and human readers, with formatting that accommodates both audiences.
key_learnings.speaker: Unidentified respondent
key_learnings.caveat: A speaker recommendation at publication, not a demonstrated performance result or a verified Adam Robinson opinion.

key_learnings.claim: Clear headings and defined sections are central to preparing documentation for AI; heading levels, emphasis and lists are suggested formatting tools.
key_learnings.speaker: Unidentified respondent
key_learnings.caveat: No comparative tests or specific formatting specification are provided.

key_learnings.claim: The respondent uses SEO as a practical analogy for documentation structure, arguing that similar formatting helps search engines, AI agents and human readers.
key_learnings.speaker: Unidentified respondent
key_learnings.caveat: This is the respondent's broad analogy; the transcript does not establish that SEO and AI retrieval requirements are identical.

key_learnings.claim: Visual content requires additional care because AI image interpretation may be limited; the respondent describes a product captioned as Finn as only beginning to interpret images.
key_learnings.speaker: Unidentified respondent
key_learnings.caveat: Product spelling and capability are unverified. The relative timing belongs to the recording context, whose date is unspecified, and should not be treated as a current product limitation. Videos are mentioned but receive no separate implementation guidance.

key_learnings.claim: Descriptive text can reduce dependence on images for both visually impaired readers and AI systems; the respondent draws on accessibility practices to explain this shared need.
key_learnings.speaker: Unidentified respondent
key_learnings.caveat: The captions refer to the American Disabilities Act and metatags. These are the source's terms, not verified legal or technical compliance guidance.

key_learnings.claim: Procedural instructions should explicitly identify the relevant interface section, action and button location. A screenshot with an arrow is insufficient on its own; accompanying text should explain where to click and what to do.
key_learnings.speaker: Unidentified respondent
key_learnings.caveat: The example concerns an add-domain button. The interface section is captioned as codec script, which may be a transcription error.

key_learnings.claim: Closing speakers recommend using their existing knowledge base and a tracking-script installation article as templates for writing support articles.
key_learnings.speaker: Unidentified closing speakers
key_learnings.caveat: The article is identified through captions as install your tracking script on support.rbdb.com. The domain, article contents and ownership are unverified; the recommendation does not establish Adam's authorship.

key_learnings.claim: A closing speaker reports that Rob created a specialized ChatGPT tool whose purpose is to optimize written posts for both humans and AI.
key_learnings.speaker: Unidentified closing speaker, referring to Rob
key_learnings.caveat: This is a report about Rob, not an Adam achievement. The tool's configuration, availability, workflow and effectiveness are not supplied.
